instruction_text: Move immediately to higher ground, upper floors of reinforced concrete multi-story buildings, or designated government flood relief shelters.
source_title: NDMA Official Flood Safety & Evacuation Protocol (2024 Revision)
source_agency: National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA) / Central Water Commission (CWC)
applicable_environment: Low-lying river basins, coastal drainage zones, urban floodplains

instruction_text: Prioritize the safe evacuation of the elderly, children, pregnant women, and persons with disabilities to elevated locations.
source_title: NDMA Official Flood Safety & Evacuation Protocol (2024 Revision)
source_agency: National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA) / Central Water Commission (CWC)

instruction_text: Do not walk, swim, cycle, or drive through flooded roads, submerged bridges, railway underpasses, or moving floodwaters.
source_title: NDMA Official Flood Safety & Evacuation Protocol (2024 Revision)
source_agency: National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA) / Central Water Commission (CWC)
applicable_environment: All flood zones, urban and rural roadways

instruction_text: Stay away from drainage canals, swollen streams, and open manholes where high-suction currents create fatal drowning hazards.
source_title: NDMA Official Flood Safety & Evacuation Protocol (2024 Revision)
source_agency: National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA) / Central Water Commission (CWC)

instruction_text: Boil all drinking water vigorously for at least 10 minutes or use certified purification tablets before consumption to prevent waterborne disease.
source_title: NDMA Official Flood Safety & Evacuation Protocol (2024 Revision)
source_agency: National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA) / Central Water Commission (CWC)

instruction_text: Discard all unpackaged food items, vegetables, and medicines that have come into direct contact with floodwaters.
source_title: NDMA Official Flood Safety & Evacuation Protocol (2024 Revision)
source_agency: National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA) / Central Water Commission (CWC)

instruction_text: Switch off the main electrical breaker and shut off LPG gas valves immediately before floodwaters enter your residence.
source_title: NDMA Official Flood Safety & Evacuation Protocol (2024 Revision)
source_agency: National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA) / Central Water Commission (CWC)

instruction_text: Maintain at least 10 meters distance from fallen power lines, submerged utility poles, and broken electrical wires.
source_title: NDMA Official Flood Safety & Evacuation Protocol (2024 Revision)
source_agency: National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA) / Central Water Commission (CWC)

instruction_text: Keep essential prescription medicines, identity documents in waterproof bags, a torch with extra batteries, and emergency supplies ready.
source_title: NDMA Official Flood Safety & Evacuation Protocol (2024 Revision)
source_agency: National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA) / Central Water Commission (CWC)

instruction_text: Follow all official emergency updates from disaster authorities and call 1077, 1070, or 112 for emergency rescue if stranded.
source_title: NDMA Official Flood Safety & Evacuation Protocol (2024 Revision)
source_agency: National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA) / Central Water Commission (CWC)

instruction_text: Evacuate immediately to designated Multi-Purpose Cyclone Shelters or fortified concrete structures upon receiving official evacuation directives.
source_title: IMD & NDMA Cyclone Preparedness, High-Wind Safety & Storm Surge Guidelines (2024)

instruction_text: Remain indoors and stay away from glass windows, unreinforced doors, and external walls during peak cyclonic winds.
source_title: IMD & NDMA Cyclone Preparedness, High-Wind Safety & Storm Surge Guidelines (2024)

instruction_text: Secure loose tin roofing sheets, asbestos panels, signage boards, and outdoor items that can become deadly flying projectiles.
source_title: IMD & NDMA Cyclone Preparedness, High-Wind Safety & Storm Surge Guidelines (2024)

instruction_text: Do not venture outdoors during the eye of the storm when winds temporarily calm; violent gale-force winds will resume abruptly from the opposite direction.
source_title: IMD & NDMA Cyclone Preparedness, High-Wind Safety & Storm Surge Guidelines (2024)

instruction_text: All fishermen and coastal vessel operators must immediately suspend maritime operations and moor vessels safely in protected harbors.
source_title: IMD & NDMA Cyclone Preparedness, High-Wind Safety & Storm Surge Guidelines (2024)

instruction_text: Charge all mobile phones, power banks, and emergency lights before power grid shutdown, and stock at least 5 days of safe drinking water.
source_title: IMD & NDMA Cyclone Preparedness, High-Wind Safety & Storm Surge Guidelines (2024)

instruction_text: If indoors during shaking, Drop, Cover, and Hold On under heavy sturdy furniture (such as a solid desk or bed) and protect your head and neck.
source_title: NDMA & USGS Earthquake Response, Structural Safety & Aftershock Protocol (2024)

instruction_text: Stay away from glass windows, heavy mirrors, unanchored bookcases, light fixtures, and exterior brick walls during ground shaking.
source_title: NDMA & USGS Earthquake Response, Structural Safety & Aftershock Protocol (2024)
applicable_environment: All buildings in seismic impact zones

instruction_text: Evacuate multi-story buildings only after ground shaking stops using designated emergency stairwells; never use elevators.
source_title: NDMA & USGS Earthquake Response, Structural Safety & Aftershock Protocol (2024)

instruction_text: If outdoors, move immediately to open ground away from high-rise buildings, utility poles, overhead power cables, and flyovers.
source_title: NDMA & USGS Earthquake Response, Structural Safety & Aftershock Protocol (2024)

instruction_text: Shut off main cooking gas cylinder valves and electric supply breakers immediately if structural damage, cracks, or gas odors are detected.
source_title: NDMA & USGS Earthquake Response, Structural Safety & Aftershock Protocol (2024)

instruction_text: Expect secondary aftershocks in the hours following the main quake; do not re-enter visibly cracked or weakened structures.
source_title: NDMA & USGS Earthquake Response, Structural Safety & Aftershock Protocol (2024)

instruction_text: Stay indoors during peak sunlight hours between 11:00 AM and 4:00 PM and minimize strenuous physical outdoor labor.
source_title: NDMA & IMD National Heatwave Action Plan & Health Protection Protocol (2024)
applicable_environment: Arid, semi-arid, and high wet-bulb temperature zones

instruction_text: Drink abundant clean water, Oral Rehydration Salts (ORS), buttermilk, lemon water, or coconut water at frequent intervals even if not feeling thirsty.
source_title: NDMA & IMD National Heatwave Action Plan & Health Protection Protocol (2024)

instruction_text: Never leave infants, young children, or pets unattended inside parked closed vehicles; vehicle cabin temperatures can reach fatal levels in minutes.
source_title: NDMA & IMD National Heatwave Action Plan & Health Protection Protocol (2024)

instruction_text: Wear lightweight, light-colored, loose-fitting cotton clothing and cover your head with a cloth, hat, or umbrella when stepping outside.
source_title: NDMA & IMD National Heatwave Action Plan & Health Protection Protocol (2024)

instruction_text: If a person displays high body temperature, confusion, dizziness, cessation of sweating, or fainting, move them to shade, apply cold water compresses, and call 108 immediately.
source_title: NDMA & IMD National Heatwave Action Plan & Health Protection Protocol (2024)

instruction_text: Evacuate hillside dwellings immediately if you observe new ground cracks, tilting trees or utility poles, sudden muddy stream runoff, or rumbling sounds.
source_title: GSI & NDMA Landslide Hazard Management & Slope Stability Guidelines (2024)
applicable_environment: Hilly terrain, mountain slopes, ghat sections

instruction_text: Evacuate uphill or laterally away from natural drainage gullies and valleys; never run downhill along the direct path of debris flow.
source_title: GSI & NDMA Landslide Hazard Management & Slope Stability Guidelines (2024)

instruction_text: Halt vehicular travel on mountain ghat roads during continuous heavy downpours and avoid parking near steep cut slopes or cliff bases.
source_title: GSI & NDMA Landslide Hazard Management & Slope Stability Guidelines (2024)

instruction_text: Evacuate immediately when directed along designated paved escape routes; do not attempt to outrun wildfire uphill or through dense uncleared brush.
source_title: NDMA & Forest Survey Wildfire Evacuation & Community Safety Protocol (2024)
source_agency: National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA) / Forest Survey of India (FSI)

instruction_text: Wear well-fitted N95/P100 respirator masks or damp cloths over mouth and nose to filter hazardous toxic smoke particles and ash.
source_title: NDMA & Forest Survey Wildfire Evacuation & Community Safety Protocol (2024)
source_agency: National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA) / Forest Survey of India (FSI)

instruction_text: Close all windows, exterior vents, and doors, and turn off household propane/gas tanks to prevent ember infiltration before evacuating.
source_title: NDMA & Forest Survey Wildfire Evacuation & Community Safety Protocol (2024)
source_agency: National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA) / Forest Survey of India (FSI)

instruction_text: If you feel a strong coastal earthquake or observe sudden rapid recession of sea water exposing the seafloor, evacuate inland and to high ground immediately without waiting for sirens.
source_title: INCOIS & NDMA Tsunami Warning Protocol & Evacuation Directives (2024)
source_agency: Indian National Centre for Ocean Information Services (INCOIS) / NDMA
applicable_environment: Coastal zones, beaches, low-lying coastal plains

instruction_text: Tsunamis consist of a series of multiple powerful wave surges spanning several hours; remain on high ground until disaster authorities issue an official all-clear.
source_title: INCOIS & NDMA Tsunami Warning Protocol & Evacuation Directives (2024)
source_agency: Indian National Centre for Ocean Information Services (INCOIS) / NDMA

instruction_text: Seek shelter immediately inside a substantial enclosed building; never seek shelter under isolated tall trees, metal sheds, or open pavilions during severe lightning.
source_title: IMD Severe Storm, Cloudburst, Squall & Lightning Safety Guidelines (2024)
applicable_environment: All storm and thunderstorm impact zones

instruction_text: In mountainous terrain, move away from dry riverbeds, stream channels, and ravines immediately upon hearing heavy continuous downpours to escape sudden cloudburst flash floods.
source_title: IMD Severe Storm, Cloudburst, Squall & Lightning Safety Guidelines (2024)

instruction_text: If instructed to shelter-in-place, move indoors immediately, seal all windows and doors with plastic sheeting or wet towels, and turn off all HVAC ventilation systems.
source_title: NDMA & MoEFCC Hazardous Materials & Chemical Spill Response Protocol (2024)
applicable_environment: Industrial zones, transport corridors, urban areas

instruction_text: If outdoor evacuation is ordered, move strictly upwind and crosswind away from the hazardous chemical release plume; cover your mouth and nose with a damp cloth.
source_title: NDMA & MoEFCC Hazardous Materials & Chemical Spill Response Protocol (2024)

instruction_text: Prioritize available stored water strictly for essential drinking, cooking, and basic hygiene; eliminate non-essential domestic and landscape water usage.
source_title: NDMA & Central Water Commission Drought Management & Conservation Protocol (2024)
applicable_environment: Drought-affected districts, agricultural and semi-arid zones
